chapter: Advice to youth and the art of drumming
title: Melodic drum solos: Sonny Payne's Old Man River and Sid Catlett
summary: A good solo follows the tune's form, as Sonny Payne's rolling through Old Man River and Catlett's melodic playing did.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Well, I've found that horn men, I had to train them that I played with -- if I was going to take a solo on something, 32-bar tune, that I would play choruses.

In your mind, you're hearing the sound of a tune. I'll tell you, what you're saying was when Sonny Payne would take his solo with Basie that time, and they would do that 'Old Man River.' Now, he would do the rolling, but he would roll practically through the whole solo. But it was through the rhythmetic pattern of the whole tune. You could follow up 'Old Man River.'
Where I learned that was listening to Sid Catlett.
Sid was the most melodic drummer I've ever heard.
